Generate Hitter Performance Report

Source: R/generatehitter.R
generate_hitter.Rd

This function fetches Statcast data for a given hitter or list of hitters, calculates key performance metrics, and generates a strike zone heatmap displaying the average exit velocity in the central zone.

Usage

generate_hitter(player_ids, start_date, end_date, game_types = c("R", "PO"))

Arguments

player_ids

A vector of numeric player IDs representing the hitters to analyze.

start_date

A character string representing the start date of the data range in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

end_date

A character string representing the end date of the data range in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

game_types

Character vector of Baseball Savant game type codes to include. Default c("R", "PO") is regular season and postseason; add "S" to include spring training.

Value

For a single ID, a ggplot object showing the central strike zone heatmap with average exit velocity (or NULL, invisibly, when no data is found). For several IDs, a named list with one such plot per hitter, named by player ID. Additionally, a table summarizing general hitting statistics is drawn for each hitter.

Details

The function performs the following for each hitter separately:

  • Fetches player names using the MLB Stats API.

  • Fetches Statcast data from Baseball Savant for the hitter and date range. Only start_date and end_date restrict the dates; there is no season filter.

  • Identifies batted balls: plate appearances ending in a hit, an in-play out, a fielder's choice, an error or a sacrifice.

  • Calculates key metrics such as average exit velocity, launch angle, hard-hit rate, strikeout rate and walk rate.

  • Creates a strike zone heatmap focusing on the central strike zone.

Definitions:

  • Plate appearances are rows with a non-empty events value, excluding baserunning events and truncated_pa.

  • Hard-hit rate = batted balls with exit velocity of 95 mph or more / batted balls with a recorded exit velocity.

  • Strikeout rate = (strikeout + strikeout_double_play) / PA. Walk rate = (walk + intent_walk) / PA.

The heatmap covers plate_x from -1 to 1 ft and plate_z from 1 to 3.5 ft in 0.5 ft cells, drawn from the catcher's view (negative plate_x is the third-base side).

Note

This function requires an active internet connection to fetch data from the MLB Stats API and Baseball Savant.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Example usage:
hitter_ids <- c(668804)  # Bryan Reynolds
start_date <- "2024-01-01"
end_date <- "2024-12-31"
generate_hitter(player_ids = hitter_ids, start_date = start_date, end_date = end_date)
#> Fetching Statcast data for batter 668804 ...


# }
